definition: Sequential minimal optimization (SMO) is an algorithm for solving the quadratic programming (QP) problem that arises during the training of support-vector machines (SVM).
details: It was invented by John Platt in 1998 at Microsoft Research. SMO is widely used for training support vector machines and is implemented by the popular LIBSVM tool. The publication of the SMO algorithm in 1998 has generated a lot of excitement in the SVM community, as previously available methods for SVM training were much more complex and required expensive third-party QP solvers.

explainer.lead: It solves the quadratic programming problem arising when training support-vector machines, making SVM training practical without third-party QP solvers.

tiers.eli5: Like fixing a big group project two people at a time instead of everyone at once.
tiers.practitioner: Widely used for training SVMs and implemented by the popular LIBSVM tool. Pitfall: it targets the specific QP problem of SVM training, not general QP.
tiers.paperLevel: An algorithm for the quadratic programming problem arising during training of support-vector machines; invented by John Platt in 1998 at Microsoft Research.

explainer.example: Training an SVM with LIBSVM, which implements SMO.
